sections.html: Corydoras diphyes was described by Axenrot and Kullander (2003). It is available only irregularly in Germany. It has a variable coloration, is comparatively easy to breed and is very suitable for the planted community tank together with peaceful companions.
Corydoras diphyes originates from a tributary of the Rio Monday, a river flowing into the Rio Parana in Paraguay.

In their natural habitat Corydoras diphyes live in large shoals together with the catfish Otocinclus mimulus. The coloration and pattern of O. mimulus match those of C. diphyes very well. In this way the Otocinclus tries to protect itself from predators, in this case Crenicichla lepidota. This phenomenon is called mimicry.

For a long time this species was known in the hobby as Corydoras flaveolus; that species, however, comes from the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo.

At first glance C. diphyes may be confused with C. paleatus, but in direct comparison the two species look quite different and can be easily told apart.
